splitProposalChirho.criteriaChirho: References to the third person of the Trinity, the Spirit of God as divine agent; contexts of empowerment, baptism, blasphemy against the Spirit
Christological title 'the Holy One of God' applied to Jesus; contexts of divine identity and messianic recognition

reasoningChirho: The description conflates two distinct theological referents: (1) the Holy Spirit as the third person of the Trinity (Matt 1:18, 3:11, Acts 1:8), and (2) 'the Holy One' as a Christological title for Jesus (Mark 1:24; John 6:69). These are separate divine persons in Trinitarian theology and should not be lumped together. The enriched description focuses almost entirely on the Spirit, yet the label includes 'the Holy One' which typically refers to Christ.

The split is defensible if covenant contexts form a distinct semantic cluster, but may be more theological than lexical.

reasoningChirho: This is H7307, a Hebrew lemma, so all 96 occurrences are Old Testament. The lemma gloss mentions 'Holy Spirit' but this appears to be anachronistic theological harmonization. The actual Hebrew contexts all refer to ruach YHWH/Elohim as a single Old Testament concept. No split is warranted—this is editorial over-reach in the gloss rather than genuine over-lumping in the sense clustering.
